text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal says Turkish ambassadors in Europe told him of their worries about Turkey weakening its ties with the West under its first Islamist prime minister. The envoys issued a similar warning to the foreign ministry.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is given a lesson on secularism in the opening ceremony of a new university.
- Erbakan by-passed the foreign ministry and held secret talks with first President of Afghanistan on Wednesday night.
- Parliament voted not take up a censure motion against the Islamist-led government on Wednesday.
- The government has prepared a new tax package.
- The opposition emphasized the importance of preventing dishonourable mistakes in the country's foriegn policy by presenting a censure motion against the government.
- Foreign minister Tansu Ciller says the budget for 1997 has the stamp of the her conservative party, the junior party in the coalition with Erbakan.
- Government plans to index civil servants' wages to the U.S. dollar constitute a trap as the depreciation of the Turkish lira against the dollar is below the rate of inflation.
- Erbakan says the censure motion has strengthened the government.
